report.summary: Checkout and sign-in failures began when the TLS certificate for auth.internal expired at 08:59:59Z. Its ACME renewal had been rejected (rate limited) since 08:05, and from 09:00:04Z checkout-service's calls to auth-service fail with PKIX 'validity check failed' errors. The error rate jumped from about 0.3% to 33.9% in the 09:00 window. The 08:54 checkout deploy (static copy changes) does not fit the symptoms: its timing is earlier, and the failure is a TLS validation error, not a change in checkout code. Health checks reported healthy because they run over plaintext port 8080, so they do not exercise the TLS path. Confidence in the certificate-expiry cause is high, but I have not checked the api-gateway logs or the certificate's own metadata, so that is a data gap.

root_cause.mechanism: The auth.internal certificate expired at 08:59:59Z after ACME renewal was rate-limited. checkout-service (and api-gateway) fail PKIX validation on each call to auth-service:8443, so token validation fails and sign-in and checkout return errors.
assumptions: The expired cert is the one served on port 8443.
Shallow health checks explain the 'healthy' status.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: The auth.internal certificate expired at 08:59:59Z after ACME renewal was rate-limited. checkout-service (and api-gateway) fail PKIX validation on each call to auth-service:8443, so token validation fails and sign-in and checkout return errors.
assumptions: The expired cert is the one served on port 8443.
Shallow health checks explain the 'healthy' status.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: The v2.15.1 deploy at 08:54 introduced an error that causes checkout failures.
assumptions: The 'static strings only' description is accurate.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: An expired certificate on payment-service's TLS path causes checkout failures, as in the 2026-06-11 incident.
assumptions: Payment-service TLS is not checked in the telemetry here.

observed_facts.statement: checkout-service error_rate was about 0.26–0.33% from 08:00 to 08:55, then 33.91% at 09:00 and 30.77–32.85% through 09:30.
auth-service logged that certificate renewal for cn=auth.internal failed (ACME order rejected, rate limited) at 08:05:03 and 08:20:17, and that the current certificate expires 2026-09-05T08:59:59Z.

checkout-service logged 'auth-service token validation failed: SSLHandshakeException: PKIX path validation failed ... validity check failed (peer auth.internal:8443)' starting at 09:00:04Z, with 45 such errors in the window.
The deploy v2.15.1 to checkout-service at 08:54:00Z was described as 'update checkout button copy and translations (static strings only)'.
checkout-service cpu (about 39–43%), memory (about 56–60%), request rate (about 82–87 req/s) and p99 latency (about 307–332 ms) stayed flat across 08:00–09:30.
The health check for auth-service is HTTP /health 200 on the plaintext admin port 8080, and all services show 'healthy' at 09:28:00Z.
A past incident (2026-06-11) had checkout 5xx errors caused by an expired TLS certificate on payment-service after a cert-manager misconfiguration.
A config change on 2026-08-31 lowered the log level for /healthz on auth-service; no other auth-service change appears in the last 7 days.

assumptions: The auth.internal certificate that expired at 08:59:59Z is the one served on auth-service port 8443 that checkout-service validates against.
The health checks do not exercise TLS, so 'healthy' does not contradict the certificate failure.
api-gateway's errors (also alerting) stem from its sync dependency on checkout-service and auth-service, though its logs were not queried.
The one card-declined and one slow-inventory log line are background noise and not part of the incident.

inferred_conclusions.statement: The auth-service certificate expired at 08:59:59Z because its ACME renewal was rate-limited and never succeeded, and this expiry is the root cause of the checkout and sign-in failures.

The checkout v2.15.1 deploy at 08:54 is unlikely to be the cause: its change is static copy, the errors are TLS validation failures, and the error rate was flat until 09:00, six minutes after the deploy.
Monitoring gap: the health checks were shallow, so the expired certificate went undetected and the service showed as healthy during the outage.

remediation.action: Immediately install a valid certificate for auth.internal (manually issue or import one, or use a fallback CA) on auth-service port 8443 and restart or reload it.
remediation.rationale: Restores TLS validation for checkout-service and api-gateway calls to auth-service.

remediation.action: Verify that checkout sign-in and checkout succeed end-to-end, and that checkout error_rate returns to about 0.3%.
remediation.rationale: Confirms recovery, since health checks are shallow.

remediation.action: Reset or back off the ACME rate limit and rerun renewal for cn=auth.internal.
remediation.rationale: Stops the cert from expiring again once the temporary certificate runs out.

remediation.action: Add certificate-expiry alerting for auth.internal and other internal certs, and alert on renewal failures.
remediation.rationale: The renewal failures from 08:05 gave about 55 minutes of warning and nobody acted on them.

remediation.action: Make health checks exercise the TLS port (8443) with a real handshake.
remediation.rationale: The plaintext admin-port check reported healthy during the outage.

remediation.action: Review renewal rate-limit handling and cert-manager configuration, following the 2026-06-11 incident.
remediation.rationale: Avoids repeat expiry from the same class of failure.

open_questions: Why did ACME renewal get rate-limited, and what caused the repeated attempts?
Do the api-gateway logs show the same PKIX errors, and what do they show for its calls to auth-service?
Is the 08:54 checkout deploy truly unrelated, or did it change anything that also touches auth calls? The change record suggests not.
Why did the auth-service /healthz log-level change on 08-31 matter, if at all?
Were any other certificates close to expiry?
